surfaces.name: tmux-ide terminal app (Home, Terminals) and background daemon (macOS arm64, Linux)
tmux-ide native macOS alpha app (separate public alpha channel)
tmux-ide CLI, stdio MCP server, SDK and control socket

claims.answer: Terminal app and daemon for macOS (Apple Silicon) and glibc Linux, plus a native macOS alpha app, a CLI and a stdio MCP server; no Windows, Intel Mac binary, browser or phone client.

desktop_os.answer: Release v2.9.25 ships darwin-arm64, linux-arm64 and linux-x64; docs say native Windows is unsupported (use WSL) and Intel Macs are not supported; README lists macOS 15+ x64, which conflicts.

mobile_apps.answer: No iOS or Android app in the release or source.

browser.answer: No browser client; a browser pane runs inside tmux.

mobile_browser.answer: No mobile access beyond tmux over SSH.

cli.answer: tmux-ide CLI with send, wait, events, team, restore, worktree, machines, automation and integration commands.

task_actions.answer: Open, steer (send, panes), answer blocked agents by jumping to them, resume and restore from the app or CLI; no review or approval UI of its own.

notifications.answer: tmux toasts, macOS and terminal banners and sound when an agent is blocked or done.

cross_device_continuity.answer: Sessions live in tmux on each machine; another device attaching sees the same toasts and the app can open remote machines over SSH.

limitations: macOS 26+ on Apple Silicon only in the release assets (README also claims macOS 15+ x64 while the docs say Intel is unsupported); native Windows unsupported; the native app is an alpha.

claims.answer: Any command in a tmux pane runs; Claude Code and opencode have first-class integrations, Codex, Cursor and Copilot have resume and detection; other agents report status with one tmux option.

harnesses.answer: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, opencode and Copilot are named for resume; any agent can join the status bus.

model_providers.answer: tmux-ide has no model layer; models are chosen in each agent.

custom_adapters.answer: An agent self-reports through tmux set-option -p @agent_state or via the fallback detector.

session_integration.answer: Agents run in plain tmux panes and tmux-ide observes them through hooks, pane options and screen manifests.

mixed_harness_operation.answer: Claude Code, Codex and opencode panes sit together in one fleet view and team.

limitations: Status is exact only for Claude Code hooks or self-reporting agents; other agents rely on screen manifests.

claims.answer: tmux-ide never touches agent credentials: each agent runs in tmux with its own login or API key; there are no credits.

agent_subscriptions.answer: Agents are the tools the user already runs in tmux, with their own logins.

api_accounts.answer: API keys are whatever the agent reads.

local_models.answer: No local-model routing; agents use their own settings.

provider_restrictions.answer: Provider restrictions are in each provider's terms.

limitations: Credentials are entirely the agent's.
claims.unknownReason: Provider terms on subscription use are outside the repository.

claims.answer: Install with one curl command or npm (bundled tmux and Node, no sudo), run tmux-ide app, and your existing tmux sessions appear; agents are started in tmux; Git is only needed for worktrees; remote machines need an installed daemon and SSH key auth.

first_task_setup.answer: curl install, tmux-ide app, then start an agent in a pane.

no_git.answer: Sessions work in any directory; git is used only by worktree commands.

local_git_without_remote.answer: Worktrees need only a local repository.

hosted_git.answer: No hosted-Git integration; worktrees are plain git.

prerequisite_guidance.answer: Getting started lists requirements and tmux version rules.

byo_vps_onboarding.answer: machines add and machines start register and start an installed remote daemon; the user installs it and sets up SSH.

limitations: Requires macOS 26+ arm64 or glibc Linux; remote hosts need tmux-ide installed first.

claims.answer: A documented CLI with --json, a daemon HTTP and socket API used by the app, a stdio MCP server and an SDK sharing one scoped read and send operation API with reservation handles; no webhooks.

cli.answer: tmux-ide commands with --json and the automation subcommands.

api.answer: The daemon serves local control, event and stream sockets to the app; only automation read and send are documented for external callers.

sdk.answer: An SDK package exposes the automation operations.

mcp_server.answer: tmux-ide mcp is a stdio MCP server for scoped pane read and send.

operations.answer: Read, send, status and wait on panes; no create, stop or review operations beyond ordinary CLI commands.

authentication.answer: Owner-only local sockets and daemon-verified invoking-pane credentials; SSH BatchMode for remote.

stability.answer: Operations are versioned and handles retry-safe; the daemon and CLI must be the same version, with no stability policy.

limitations: Automation can read and send to panes only; it cannot create sessions or approve through MCP; daemon version must match.

claims.answer: Lua plugins add commands to the palette with consent and resource limits, the Claude Code hook integration and bundled skill are installed on request, and MCP exposes pane read and send; MCP servers for agents are the agents' own.

mcp_client.answer: tmux-ide is not an MCP client.

plugins.answer: Lua plugins from ~/.tmux-ide/plugins after plugin consent.

custom_tools.answer: Plugins and tmux-ide action add commands that can run allowed programs and drive panes.

instructions_import.answer: integration install claude refreshes a bundled Claude skill.

permission_scope.answer: Plugins run in the daemon host with time limits and a memory cap and programs you allow.

integration_owner.answer: Agents own their MCP clients; tmux-ide owns its hooks and plugin host.

limitations: No MCP client; plugin API is local Lua.

implementation_evidence.answer: docs/content/docs/native-alpha.mdx and the repository layout at the pinned commit.

claims.answer: A product-shipped Claude Code skill plus the send, wait, events and team --json commands (also over MCP and SDK) let an agent task other running agents, read the fleet and wait for results across harnesses; tmux-ide designates no lead or orchestrator role, its README says it shows and connects agents and does not orchestrate them, and Claude Code agent teams are Claude's own feature that it displays.

roles.answer: Panes can carry role names and team assignments; no orchestration roles.

messages.answer: send types into another agent's prompt.

results_return.answer: wait on output or status and read panes; no structured result.

activation.answer: Commands are always available once installed.

live_progress.answer: events --follow and team --json show live status.

claims.answer: No scheduler or triggers; notifications and events fire when agents change state; the daemon keeps snapshots every 30 seconds.

claims.answer: Steer by typing in panes or send, close panes, restore after crashes, and get notifications when agents are blocked or done with a jump to the one that needs you; no pause or approval routing.
